name: Iron Law of Processor Performance

variables.name: CPU Execution Time
variables.description: Total active processor time spent executing the program.

variables.name: Instruction Count
variables.description: Dynamic number of retired instructions executed by the program.

variables.name: Cycles Per Instruction
variables.description: Average clock cycles consumed per completed instruction.

variables.name: Instructions Per Cycle
variables.description: Reciprocal of CPI (1 / CPI); throughput per clock tick.

variables.name: Clock Period
variables.description: Duration of one synchronous clock cycle (1 / f).

variables.name: Clock Frequency
variables.description: Clock oscillation rate (cycles per second).

assumptions: Measures active CPU execution time assuming constant average clock frequency f and excluding external I/O stall waits.
applicability: Comparing ISA efficiency (IC), microarchitectural throughput (CPI/IPC), and silicon timing (f) across processor designs.
workedExample: TIAN-ISA v1 canonical 4-instruction program: IC = 4, CPI = 6 (sequential 6-stage model) -> 24 simulated cycles. At f = 2.0 GHz (0.5 ns period), T_exec = 24 * 0.5 ns = 12.0 ns.

name: CMOS Dynamic Switching Power

variables.name: Dynamic Switching Power
variables.description: Average power dissipated charging and discharging logic node capacitances.

variables.name: Activity Factor
variables.description: Fraction of switching transitions per clock cycle.

variables.name: Switched Load Capacitance
variables.description: Total capacitive load of transistors and interconnect wires driven.

variables.name: Supply Voltage
variables.description: Core supply rail potential.

variables.name: Clock Frequency
variables.description: Switching clock rate.

assumptions: Models capacitive switching energy in digital CMOS circuits; total package power also adds static leakage (I_leak * V_DD) and short-circuit current.
applicability: Explains DVFS voltage-frequency scaling and why modest voltage reductions yield quadratic power savings.
workedExample: If alpha = 0.25, C = 10 nF, V_DD = 1.0 V, f = 3.0 GHz -> P_dyn = 0.25 * 10e-9 * 1.0^2 * 3e9 = 7.5 W. Lowering V_DD to 0.8 V reduces P_dyn by 36% to 4.8 W at the same frequency.

name: Average Memory Access Time (AMAT — Two-Level)

variables.name: Average Memory Access Time
variables.description: Expected latency per memory reference across the hierarchy.

variables.name: L1 Hit Time
variables.description: Access latency when data hits in L1 cache.

variables.name: L1 Local Miss Rate
variables.description: Fraction of L1 accesses that miss and query L2.

variables.name: L2 Hit Time
variables.description: Access latency when data hits in L2 cache.

variables.name: L2 Local Miss Rate
variables.description: Fraction of L2 queries that miss and go to lower memory.

variables.name: L2 Miss Penalty
variables.description: Penalty to retrieve cache line from L3/DRAM on L2 miss.

assumptions: Assumes serial single-outstanding lookup without hardware prefetching or store-buffer hiding; extends recursively to L3 and DRAM.
applicability: Quantifying cache hit-rate vs. capacity latency trade-offs in memory hierarchy design.
workedExample: Given T_hit,L1 = 4 cycles, MR_L1 = 0.05, T_hit,L2 = 12 cycles, MR_L2 = 0.20, T_miss,L2 = 180 cycles -> AMAT = 4 + 0.05 * (12 + 0.20 * 180) = 4 + 0.05 * 48 = 6.4 cycles.

name: Amdahl's Law (Parallel Speedup Bound)

variables.name: Overall Speedup Factor
variables.description: Ratio of original single-unit execution time to enhanced execution time.

variables.name: Parallelizable Fraction
variables.description: Proportion of original execution time eligible for speedup.

variables.name: Local Speedup Factor
variables.description: Speedup applied to the parallelizable portion (e.g., N ideal cores).

assumptions: Assumes fixed workload size (strong scaling), zero synchronization/coherence overhead, and ideal load balance.
applicability: Evaluating diminishing returns when adding cores or vector lanes to workloads with serial bottlenecks.
workedExample: If 80% of a workload is parallelizable (p = 0.80) across s = 8 ideal cores -> S_overall = 1 / (0.20 + 0.80 / 8) = 1 / 0.30 = 3.33x (asymptotic ceiling as s -> inf is 5.0x).

name: Thermal Junction Temperature Model (1D Steady-State)

variables.name: Silicon Junction Temperature
variables.description: Steady-state transistor junction temperature on the active die.

variables.name: Ambient Temperature
variables.description: Cooling air or fluid inlet temperature.

variables.name: Thermal Power Dissipation
variables.description: Steady-state heat flux generated by the processor package.

variables.name: Junction-to-Ambient Thermal Resistance
variables.description: Series thermal resistance across die, TIM, IHS, and heatsink.

assumptions: Simplified lumped 1D steady-state thermal resistance network; localized core hotspots require 3D spatial thermal mapping.
applicability: Estimating thermal envelope headroom and cooling solution requirements under sustained TDP load.
workedExample: At T_A = 25 deg C, P = 120 W, and R_theta,JA = 0.45 deg C/W -> T_J = 25 + 120 * 0.45 = 79 deg C.

name: Synchronous Clock Timing Constraint

variables.name: Minimum Clock Period
variables.description: Shortest valid clock cycle before setup timing violations occur.

variables.name: Clock-to-Q Propagation Delay
variables.description: Delay from rising clock edge until launching flip-flop output stabilizes.

variables.name: Critical Combinational Path Delay
variables.description: Longest propagation path through combinational logic gates.

variables.name: Flip-Flop Setup Time
variables.description: Time data must remain stable before the capturing clock edge.

variables.name: Clock Skew
variables.description: Worst-case arrival timing difference across the clock distribution network.

assumptions: Setup timing constraint for single-phase rising-edge-triggered synchronous digital logic.
applicability: Determining maximum clock frequency (f_max = 1 / T_clk,min) and motivating pipeline stage subdivision.
workedExample: If t_pcq = 35 ps, t_comb,max = 240 ps, t_setup = 25 ps, t_skew = 20 ps -> T_clk,min = 320 ps, giving f_max = 1 / 320 ps = 3.125 GHz.
